title.value: Protocol for fever control using external cooling in mechanically ventilated patients with septic shock: SEPSISCOOL II randomised controlled trial
title.justification: The title is clearly stated at the top of the document and repeated several times throughout.
title.quote: Protocol for fever control using external cooling in mechanically ventilated patients with septic shock: SEPSISCOOL II randomised controlled trial

analysis.description: This study investigates the effectiveness of fever control at normothermia using external cooling in mechanically ventilated patients with septic shock. The key aim is to assess if controlling fever can improve organ failure outcomes and reduce mortality within 60 days among patients experiencing septic shock. It's structured as a multicenter, open-label, adaptive, randomized controlled trial involving 820 patients.

type.justification: The study involves a pragmatic, multicenter, open-label randomized controlled trial evaluating real-world interventions in a clinical setting, which characterizes empirical research.
type.quote: SEPSISCOOL II is a pragmatic, investigator-­initiated, adaptive, multicentre, open-­label, randomised controlled, superiority trial in patients admitted to the intensive care unit with febrile septic shock.

name.justification: The research primarily addresses a medical question regarding treatment strategies for fever in septic shock, which is a significant concern in clinical medicine.
name.quote: This study will compare two strategies within the first 48 hours of septic shock: treatment of fever with cooling or no treatment of fever.
